name: Is it worth changing from a single bathroom vanity to a double vanity?

mainEntity.name: Is it worth changing from a single bathroom vanity to a double vanity?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Replacing a single vanity with a double vanity is possible only when the room has adequate wall length, circulation space, and a plumbing layout that can support two basins. The cabinet, countertop, sinks, faucets, mirror, lighting, drain connections, and storage plan all need to be considered together.

Context: A double vanity can improve shared use, but it may reduce clearance or leave less space for doors and other fixtures. Elite Remodeling & Design can evaluate the proposed arrangement through bathroom design and construction planning rather than selecting the cabinet in isolation.

Key factors:
- Available wall width and door swing
- Two drain and supply connections
- Countertop seam and sink placement
- Lighting and mirror coverage

Practical guidance: Mark the cabinet footprint on the floor with tape before purchasing. Check drawer operation, knee space, and access to shutoff valves.

The best choice balances shared convenience with usable circulation and service access.
acceptedAnswer.description: A double vanity can help a shared bathroom, but only if the wall length, circulation, storage, lighting, and plumbing support it. Tape the proposed footprint on the floor and confirm two sink connections before ordering.
